title: Kubernetes 1.37 Released: Stable Metrics API  and Rootless Kubelet in Beta
gist: Kubernetes 1.37 'Garhwal' ships 67 enhancements centred on stability, security and AI/ML workload optimization, including a generally available Metrics API, beta rootless kubelet enabled by default, beta HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale-to-zero aimed at GPU cost, and GA resilient watchcache initialization that stops kube-apiserver from flooding etcd on restart.

insights.claim: Kubernetes 1.37, named 'Garhwal', contains 67 enhancements: 27 alpha features, 23 graduating to beta, 16 becoming generally available or stable, and a single deprecation or removal.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: A 16-to-1 ratio of graduations to removals signals a maturing platform where upgrade risk is falling, lowering the cost of staying current.

insights.claim: The next Kubernetes release, version 1.38, is expected by December 2026, keeping the project on its roughly quarterly cadence.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Predictable release timing is what lets platform teams and vendors plan support matrices and certification cycles.

insights.claim: The metrics.k8s.io Metrics API reached general availability, providing the common node and pod health measurement layer that Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Vertical Pod Autoscaler and kubectl top depend on.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Stabilising the metrics substrate removes a long-standing dependency risk for every autoscaling and cost-optimisation product built on Kubernetes.
insights.locator: One of the main features in version 1.37

insights.claim: HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale-to-zero graduated to beta and is enabled by default, explicitly framed as a cost reduction for AI/ML workloads that require GPUs in cloud environments.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Native idle-to-zero for GPU pods attacks the single biggest line item in AI inference bills and pressures serverless-GPU vendors selling that capability.
insights.locator: In Kubernetes 1.37, HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale to zero

insights.claim: A new alpha feature gate, InPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption, lets the scheduler free resources on a node at capacity by preempting low-priority workloads so that pending in-place resizes of high-priority applications can proceed.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Workload-aware preemption is how clusters get packed denser - the mechanism behind utilisation gains that translate directly into infrastructure savings.
insights.locator: Alpha features in this release include workload-aware scheduling

insights.claim: Running the kubelet in a Linux user namespace graduated to beta with the KubeletInUserNamespace feature gate enabled by default, letting core node components run as non-root on the host specifically to reduce the impact of container escape attacks.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Default-on rootless node components shrink the blast radius that container-security vendors have been selling against.
insights.locator: Also, Kubelet in the user namespace or Rootless mode

insights.claim: Pod certificates graduated to stable, giving Kubernetes native support for secure pod-to-pod communication without relying on external tools to bootstrap mTLS between internal services.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: In-tree mTLS bootstrapping erodes a core value proposition of service-mesh and certificate-management add-ons.
insights.locator: In addition, pod certificates graduated to stable

insights.claim: Pod-level checkpoint and restore lets the kubelet snapshot a running container's memory and process trees and restore the pod from it, aimed at debugging and security analysis.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Live-process forensics in-cluster is a new primitive for incident response and for migrating stateful or long-warm AI workloads.
insights.locator: The new pod-level checkpoint and restore feature

insights.claim: Before resilient watchcache initialization, a kube-apiserver restart or lost cache connection in a large cluster would flood etcd with requests, causing performance degradation and potential control plane outages.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Names the specific thundering-herd mechanism behind many large-cluster outages - a recurring root cause worth checking in post-incident reports.
insights.locator: Resilient watchcache initialization became generally available

insights.claim: With resilient watchcache initialization generally available and enabled by default, kube-apiserver now safely delegates bounded requests and rejects the rest with HTTP 429 responses instead of overwhelming etcd.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Backpressure by default makes very large clusters materially safer to operate, supporting continued consolidation onto fewer, bigger clusters.
insights.quote: Resilient watchcache initialization is stable and locked on so that the kube-apiserver no longer floods etcd at startup.

insights.claim: A Recreate strategy for StatefulSet rollouts entered alpha, off by default, deleting all existing pods to allow clean recovery from stuck or pending pods during updates without manual pod deletion.
insights.speaker: Mostafa Radwan
insights.so_what: Reduces the manual toil that keeps stateful workloads off Kubernetes, incrementally expanding its addressable workload set.
insights.locator: Another feature entering alpha is the Recreate strategy
